**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.html#/part-3-data-management-and-the-reproduction){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).

Part 3 is where the R work reaches its target. It starts with the data management that every analysis of the case needs, then sets out what the five Multi100 analysts did with the claim, and you reproduce one of their analyses from the public file of the original study. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. Data management

**On the slides.** The slides present the public file of the original authors (OAs) and the course file built from it, each with a codebook beside it. They then set out the three things that a missing value means in these data, and the difference between raw files, scripts and derived files.

## 2. The five analysts

**On the slides.** The five Multi100 analysts are placed by their gaps in percentage points, and a table then sets out what each of them did.

## 3. The instruction of Multi100

**On the slides.** The slides read the instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 word for word and show what it left open. They then set the aim of the reproduction, which is one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose.

## 4. Task 3 – The reproduction

[Open the browser lab at Task 3](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

If you work in the workspace, use your report or `prep/reproduce_reanalyses.R` instead. Choose one of the five analysts and complete their cell on the public file `audit_original.csv`. Four of them have a value that Multi100 recorded: $\chi^2$ = 14.265 for 8PTRZ, z = −3.771 for UYV3F, z = 3.645 for EWFMI and $\chi^2$ = 13.683 for 25N5D. P9W8Y has none, so its test of three groups, $\chi^2$ = 15.951 on 2 degrees of freedom, can be run again but not matched. Every one of them filters, recodes or splits a column of the public file first. Type the analyst and the value in the chat without sending them, and send them when the facilitator says go.

## 5. The defaults of the software

**On the slides.** `chisq.test()` and `prop.test()` apply the continuity correction to a two-by-two table unless they are told otherwise. The slides also show the base group that sets the sign of the z of EWFMI, and why everyone who chose the same analyst got the same value while the five analysts, each writing their own code, did not.

## 6. A second reproduction

[Open the browser lab at Task 3](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Reproduce a second analyst whose analysis differs from your first in one decision. Compare the data work that the two need, and their gaps in percentage points.

**By the end of the part** you can read a codebook, tell the three kinds of missing value in the data apart, and say why the raw file is never edited by hand, and you have reproduced one or two of the five reanalyses from the public file yourself.
